sample_unit: LLM calls (125 synthetic cases x 5 models x 3 runs)

links.outcome: Agreement of LLM rankings across scoring constructs and with expert adequacy ratings
links.effect: Recall, alarm-burden proxy and WCS gave three different model orderings; WCS showed no positive association with blinded expert adequacy (rho -0.17, p=0.41) despite strong inter-rater concordance (rho 0.977).
links.quote: In the expert substudy, inter-rater concordance was strong (rho 0.977), but WCS did not show a positive association with expert adequacy (rho -0.17, p=0.41).

links.outcome: Whether algorithmic scoring against reference standards agrees with blinded expert adequacy ratings
links.effect: Rankings were discordant across scoring constructs; WCS did not correlate positively with expert adequacy (rho -0.17), supporting use of multiple evaluation methods including blinded expert ratings.

unlisted_practices: Report algorithmic benchmark metrics alongside blinded expert adequacy ratings before deployment decisions
Use trap-embedded synthetic cases to test whether LLMs catch embedded errors in prescription review

screen.reason: The study evaluates the performance and ranking metrics of multiple LLMs on a synthetic benchmark of peritoneal dialysis prescription review with trap cases and compares algorithmic metrics to blinded expert adequacy evaluations.
